title: The Last Alibi
tagline: To clear her name, she must prove she was with the victim.
logline: A disgraced defense attorney becomes the prime suspect in her former mentor's murder and has one night to recover the missing hour that could save—or condemn—her.
synopsis: Nora Vale wakes in a closed courthouse with blood on her sleeve and no memory of the previous hour. Her mentor is dead in chambers, the security archive has been cut, and someone has filed a sealed confession in Nora's name. Hunted by the detective who ended her career, Nora follows courtroom clues that turn every old client into a suspect. The audience decides which testimony she trusts and which dangerous truth becomes canon.

world.setting: A rain-locked downtown courthouse after midnight, from marble courtrooms and evidence vaults to maintenance tunnels beneath the old records wing.
rules: The courthouse seals automatically until dawn because the security system records an active threat.
Every recovered camera clip is authentic, but at least one has been moved to the wrong timestamp.
Nora's missing hour returns only in sensory fragments triggered by evidence she physically handled.

visualStyle.camera: Tight handheld suspicion, severe courthouse symmetry, and rapid vertical rack-focus reveals from evidence in the foreground to a watcher behind Nora.
visualStyle.lighting: Cold emergency strips cross warm pools from desk lamps; lightning flashes briefly expose figures behind textured courtroom glass.
visualStyle.wardrobe: Nora's cream blouse and black trousers accumulate visible evidence, while Silas stays controlled in a rain-dark detective coat and Elias appears in archival charcoal suits.

characters.name: Nora Vale
characters.role: disgraced defense attorney and primary suspect
characters.objective: Recover her missing hour, clear her name, and expose why her mentor destroyed her career.
characters.flaw: She cross-examines people she loves instead of admitting when she needs them.
characters.secret: Nora came to the courthouse intending to steal a sealed case file from her mentor.
visualCues: courtroom poise that fractures around music

characters.name: Silas Reed
characters.objective: Keep Nora alive long enough to determine whether she is victim, witness, or killer.
characters.flaw: He mistakes emotional distance for impartial judgment.
characters.secret: Silas removed one piece of evidence from Nora's disbarment case because it implicated his father.
visualCues: a healed cut matching Nora's broken watch

characters.name: June Park
characters.role: court archivist and Nora's closest friend
characters.objective: Open the sealed archive before police backup arrives and preserve the truth it contains.
characters.flaw: She protects people by editing the choices available to them.
characters.secret: June created the false timestamp system years ago at Elias's request.
visualCues: ink numbers written along her wrist

characters.name: Elias Wren
characters.role: victim, mentor, and unseen architect of the night
characters.objective: Force Nora to finish the corruption case he was too compromised to prosecute.
characters.flaw: He turns people into pieces of evidence and calls the manipulation mentorship.
characters.secret: Elias scheduled messages to be released after his death, including contradictory confessions from himself.
visualCues: voice heard through old dictation machines

seasonArc.premise: Across the locked-down night, every audience choice determines which witness Nora trusts and which evidence she sacrifices, producing a coherent but variable path to the killer.
seasonArc.stakes: At dawn the courthouse unlocks, Nora is arrested, and a corruption archive capable of freeing innocent clients is automatically destroyed.
endingTargets: Nora proves the visible murder scene was staged after Elias died elsewhere.
The audience-selected ally supplies Nora's final alibi but demands a personal reckoning.
A scheduled message reveals Elias expected Nora to become the last suspect standing.

episodes.title: Blood in Chambers
episodes.logline: Nora wakes beside her murdered mentor as the courthouse locks and her own signed confession prints downstairs.
storyBeats: Nora follows a ringing evidence phone into chambers and discovers Elias dead behind the bench.
Silas arrives before official dispatch and refuses to explain how he entered the sealed building.
A clerk's printer produces Nora's confession with details only the killer should know.
episodes.cliffhanger: Security footage shows Nora entering chambers twice—once in the clothes she wears and once in a red dress she has never seen.
episodes.generationPrompt: Create a rain-soaked locked-courthouse murder mystery with intimate evidence close-ups, charged distrust between former lovers, and a final surveillance reveal of two versions of the heroine.

vote.question: Which clue should Nora pursue before the archive locks?

options.label: Trace the red dress
options.consequence: Nora searches judicial robing rooms and risks meeting the impersonator.
options.generationDirective: Follow the red-dress trail through mirrored robing rooms with identity-driven suspense.

options.label: Test the confession
options.consequence: Nora and Silas examine the signature, forcing them to revisit their broken engagement.
options.generationDirective: Center a forensic signature test with former lovers working inches apart under mounting distrust.

episodes.title: The Missing Minute
episodes.logline: A recovered clip clears Nora for fifty-nine minutes but places June with Elias during the only minute that matters.
storyBeats: Nora discovers every courthouse clock skipped from 11:16 to 11:18 during a maintenance reset.
June admits she moved one timestamp but insists Elias ordered it before his death.
Silas finds Nora's broken watch embedded with a voice recording from the missing minute.
episodes.cliffhanger: The recording captures Nora saying, 'If I remember this, we all go to prison,' before a gunshot.
episodes.generationPrompt: Use conflicting clocks, archive aisles, and a broken-watch recording to compress a legal thriller into one missing minute, ending on the heroine's own incriminating voice.

vote.question: Who hears the full recording first?

options.label: Trust Silas
options.consequence: Silas gains context that may clear Nora while obtaining evidence he is duty-bound to use.
options.generationDirective: Play the complete recording with Silas in a dark courtroom and let professional duty collide with intimacy.

options.label: Trust June
options.consequence: June can decode the timestamp but may erase the file to protect the archive.
options.generationDirective: Play the recording in the archive lab as June controls the only copy and reveals technical knowledge.

episodes.title: Objection, Hearsay
episodes.logline: Elias's posthumous deposition names Nora as both his killer and the only lawyer capable of proving he lied.
storyBeats: A projector starts Elias's prerecorded testimony when Nora enters Courtroom Four.
He describes the murder scene accurately, then points out one physical detail that has changed.
Nora realizes the body was moved after the security lockdown began.
episodes.cliffhanger: The original crime scene is beneath the jury box, where someone trapped inside begins pounding for help.
episodes.generationPrompt: Stage a posthumous courtroom deposition that feels like a duel between mentor and student, reveal a changed murder detail, and finish with pounding beneath the jury box.

vote.question: Should Nora open the jury box or preserve the scene?

options.label: Open it now
options.consequence: Nora may save a witness but destroys the cleanest path to reconstructing the murder.
options.generationDirective: Open the hidden compartment immediately and prioritize a desperate live rescue over pristine evidence.

options.label: Preserve the scene
options.consequence: Nora documents the evidence while the trapped person's voice grows dangerously weak.
options.generationDirective: Force Nora to document each clue against a visible countdown as the unseen witness fades.
